Question: I like physics and chemestry. Which Engineering sub should I take?
Answer: I am assuming that you are thinking about it based on your observation and experience in high school. Firstly, you should see the actual curriculum of physics and chemistry followed in engineering streams. It is not always similar to the physics and chemistry taught in high school. Different Streams of engineering are focused on different aspects of Physics and Chemistry. You might not like the actual topics covered in these degrees. Secondly, Try to imagine yourself working with a degree in your desired field. Will you be able to work in that environment? Will you be happy with a profession in that engineering stream? Will you be happy in the profession? If your answer was yes to these questions, then you already know which field to choose. Thirdly, perform some research on the scope of your chosen field of engineering in the future. If the scope is not much, Please try not to go for it. For example, the field of Petrochemical engineering is expected to have very less scope in future due to inclination of world towards renewable energy. Fourthly, consider the amount of competition in your chosen field of engineering before finalizing it. For example, the field of Computer engineering is becoming saturated with every passing year, even though there is a massive increase in employment opportunities in that field. Finally, i would like to say that you can excel in any field of engineering, given that you are passionate about it and ready to work hard

Question: How hard are the SAT subject tests?
Answer: Having scored 800 in Math 2, Chemistry and Physics, I feel qualified to answer this question. SAT Math is fairly tough, I would say. It is not that difficult to score a perfect 800, but it still requires a lot of practice to do so. You should have a good command over your calculator and its functions. You normally need 42–44 correct answers out of 50 in it to get a perfect score, depending on the difficulty of the test. To ace it, you just need to have good basics, knowledge of all the formulae and the practice of the different types of test questions. Time management is very important in this test SAT Chemistry is a bit tricky one. Though the questions are easier, but you need to get about 79–81 questions out of 85 correct to get a 800 in it. It requires a thorough knowledge of the concepts to ace it. The assertion and the reasoning part of the test is a bit confusing. The rest of the questions are fairly easy. Just don’t make silly mistakes! SAT Physics is the most difficult among them, but it also has a much better score curve. You need about 59 correct answers out of 75 to get a perfect score. You definitely need to learn the formulae for this one. It tests your conceptual knowledge completely. Practice tests are the most important part of any SAT Subject test preparation
